styleBrief:
This climate tech landscape analysis demands a stark, data-driven aesthetic that matches the urgency and gravity of the subject matter. Use dark backgrounds—deep charcoal or black—as the primary canvas to create a sense of environmental crisis and technical sophistication. Against these dark foundations, deploy bright accent colors strategically: electric blues for breakthrough technologies, sharp greens for commercial successes, and warning oranges or reds for barriers and constraints. This high-contrast approach should feel authoritative and urgent, like reading a critical intelligence briefing under emergency lighting.

Every card must integrate dense statistical information seamlessly into flowing prose using the stats smart layout variant. When presenting breakthrough cost declines, investment figures, or production scales, embed these numbers as hero statistics within explanatory paragraphs—never let data stand naked without interpretation. Use the outlineBoxes smart layout sparingly and only for structural comparisons like the four key sectors or three systemic barriers. The typography should emphasize hierarchy through bold H1 titles that read like authoritative declarations, with H4 subheaders in columns breaking up dense technical prose. Employ strategic color spans on critical metrics and breakthrough moments—highlight "$165 billion," "89% cost decline," and "sub-$100 per ton" in accent colors to make the data visceral and immediate. Blockquotes should capture industry voices that validate the analysis, set against accent backgrounds to break the rhythm of technical density. Avoid any presentation-style flourishes—no solid boxes, no decorative elements. This document should read like an authoritative technical report where every visual choice reinforces the message that climate technology has reached a pivotal, urgent moment demanding immediate attention and investment.
